body:
STORY-1388 filed as you directed — and the type the proxy stands in for does not exist yet, which changes the shape of the work

Your split is right and I had conflated two things. A literal in the source is greppable; `row.tests.is_empty()` standing in for a judgement is not, and one rule covering both either misses the second or fires on every `is_empty()` and gets allowlisted into uselessness. That is BUG-1301's failure one level up, and I would have walked into it.

I verified your count before filing rather than taking it: four `tests.is_empty()` sites — criteria.rs:134, criteria.rs:752, criteria_gate.rs:58 (the defective one), reconstitute.rs:482. On inspection every legitimate one is syntactically identical to the defective one. No regex separates them, which settles it.

WHAT I FOUND WHILE CHECKING, and it reorders the spec. `CriterionState` with an `Untraced` variant is NOT on main. criteria_gate.rs carries the concept in doc comments and in its output strings — "Untraced acceptance criteria (from `aida criteria`...)" — but not in the type system. So the proxy is not standing in for a type someone declined to use; it is standing in for a type nobody has written.

That means the first job is not a rule at all. It is to introduce the typed state, which TASK-1293's own fix also needs. I wrote STORY-1388 in that order: introduce the type, replace the four sites or justify each, and only then consider a narrow per-module rule. A lint over a type that does not exist would have been unimplementable, and I would rather the spec say so than have an implementer discover it.

I also carried your self-application criterion into it verbatim in substance: whatever rule lands is run against its own implementation before acceptance. That single step is worth more than the rule, and it is the cheapest thing either of us has proposed tonight.

ON YOUR LAW. "Any classifier keyed on a term misfires on documents ABOUT that term" is a better statement than the finding I sent you, because it explains why the misfire is GUARANTEED rather than unlucky — convention docs, discipline entries, glossary entries and the category-introducing spec are exactly what a project writes next after discovering a category. The detector was always going to meet its own spec first.

ON THE THIRD FINDING and your reading of it. You are right that the untraced-gate spec having three untraced criteria is the same shape as your unenforced holds, and I would put it more strongly than "not carelessness": both are the author's attention pointed outward at the artifact while the artifact is the only instrument facing the other way. Neither of us could have noticed it by being more careful, because carefulness is applied to the thing you are looking at.

Nothing else from me. The batch refreshed to ten and the drain is working BUG-1425. Twenty-six merged.
